GoatCitadel Product and engineering overview
What It Does Features Mission Control Architecture Trust

GoatCitadel

A local-first AI operations console that brings chat, serious multi-step AI work, code assistance, memory, tools, approvals, and integrations into one understandable workspace.

A pnpm monorepo with a Fastify gateway, React Mission Control Next shell, shared contracts, policy/orchestration/storage packages, durable execution, provider routing, and operator-visible runtime truth.

See Mission Control Review capabilities DeepWiki reference
3 Primary work surfaces: Chat, Cowork, and Code
7 Current 1.0 navigation areas in Mission Control Next
30+ Gateway route-service families behind the product
1.0 Release posture anchored by named verification lanes

High Level

What GoatCitadel is

Think of it as a command center for working with AI: simple when you need a quick answer, structured when the job needs planning, and careful when the AI wants to touch files, tools, money, or external services.

GoatCitadel separates UI, gateway, contracts, storage, policy, memory, skills, and orchestration so the same runtime can power different operator surfaces without duplicating execution logic.

Chat

The fast lane for conversation, drafting, questions, attachments, and lightweight help.

Mission-session chat with threaded history, model/provider routing, attachments, generated artifacts, trace visibility, memory context, and streaming status.

Cowork

The guided work lane for research, planning, task breakdowns, approvals, and multi-step AI execution.

Delegation-first surface backed by orchestration runs, durable run linkage, task state, operator action prompts, run maps, and checkpoint visibility.

Code

The technical work lane for repo-aware implementation, patch review, validation commands, and code assistance with human control.

Repo-bound workbench with project binding, worktree creation, file tree, editor/diff panes, patch export, helper snippets, validation commands, and governed Code Mode.

Feature inventory

This is the plain-English catalog of what the product can do today, grouped by the way a user experiences it.

This list is grounded in the current route model, README, release evidence, gateway route services, and shared package layout.

C Conversation

Chat threads

Ask questions, draft content, attach files, switch models, and keep the conversation moving.

Threaded chat sessions with model routing, attachment handling, turn traces, queued sends, streaming, and generated artifacts.

W Orchestration

Cowork runs

Turn open-ended work into visible steps, blockers, decisions, and next actions.

Agentic run views, workflow state, plan/run-map/timeline tabs, task board integration, and approval-linked continuation.

D Development

Code workbench

Use AI to inspect and modify code without losing sight of files, diffs, and tests.

Project import, worktree state, file tree, Monaco editor, selected/repo diffs, command output, patch application/export, and run artifacts.

Project containers

Group related Chat, Cowork, and Code threads around one project or workspace.

Project route support, session project binding, workspace paths, route-preserved thread context, and source binding into Code.

M Memory

Memory and context

Let the system remember useful context while keeping memory visible and manageable.

Memory lifecycle services, memory items, QMD context packs, learned-memory policy, maintenance runs, provenance, and write-gate evidence.

S Skills

Reusable skills

Package repeatable workflows so the AI can apply known playbooks instead of improvising every time.

A Approvals

Human gates

Risky actions wait for a person, with context about what is being requested and why.

T Tools

Tool policy

File, shell, browser, HTTP, and communication actions are governed instead of hidden behind blind automation.

See whether the gateway, daemon, backups, local runtimes, approvals, and spend are healthy.

Connect communication channels and external systems without pretending every connector has the same maturity.

V Voice and media

Multimodal work

Attach images and files, transcribe audio, speak responses, and generate or inspect artifacts from a thread.

Architecture

How the system is organized

GoatCitadel is built so the visible product, the AI runtime, and the safety systems can grow without becoming one fragile ball of code.

The repo is a pnpm workspace with release-bearing apps, shared libraries, route-service facades, contracts, storage repositories, verification scripts, templates, and packaging automation.

User surfaces

Mission Control Next

The interface people use: Chat, Cowork, Code, Projects, Library, Ops, and Settings.

`apps/mission-control-next`, shared UI components, threaded-surface-core, route model, visual baselines, and shell access gate.

Control plane

Fastify Gateway

The brain that handles model calls, tools, approvals, memory, integrations, diagnostics, and runtime state.

`apps/gateway` route services wrap chat, LLM, approvals, tools, durable, memory, MCP, files, settings, integrations, runtime, costs, and verification APIs.

Shared core

Packages

Reusable building blocks that keep policy, memory, storage, skills, and orchestration consistent.

`packages/contracts`, `storage`, `policy-engine`, `orchestration`, `memory-core`, `skills`, `gateway-core`, `mesh-core`, and `extensions-sdk`.

Apps

Runtime entry points

Mission Control is the operator console, Gateway is the local service, Desktop packages the experience, and the former NPU sidecar path is retired from shipped 1.0 local inference work.

`apps/mission-control-next` is canonical 1.0; `apps/mission-control` is compatibility-only; `apps/gateway` is Fastify; `apps/mission-control-windows` is the WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK host; `apps/mission-control-desktop` is Tauri rollback / experimental macOS packaging; NPU sidecar support is retired from the shipped 1.0 source and installer.

Gateway

Runtime APIs

The gateway turns user requests into model calls, tool checks, memory lookups, approvals, and status updates.

Route-service families include chat, messages, sessions, delegate, LLM, tools, approvals, durable, runtime lifecycle, knowledge, memory, MCP, integrations, costs, files, settings, workspaces, voice, media, and health.

Storage

Durable state

Chats, runs, approvals, memory, backups, and audit data survive across restarts.

SQLite/Postgres repositories, protected migrations, chat session metadata, turn traces, durable runs, approval effects, memory contexts, and backup manifests anchor the runtime.

Packaging

Installable desktop path

Windows users can install and launch GoatCitadel as a desktop app with local runtime management.

Windows x64/arm64 bundle targets, WinUI 3 desktop host, launcher commands, Inno Setup installers, embedded Node verification, and silent install/uninstall smoke are documented.

Trust Model

Why this is safer than a black-box agent

GoatCitadel is designed to show the user what is happening, ask before risky actions, and avoid pretending experimental areas are production guarantees.

The current 1.0 posture distinguishes canonical state from derived UI, release proof from evidence, callable capabilities from inspectable candidates, and trusted-code Code Mode from hostile-code sandboxing.

Visible routing Provider, model, runtime, fallback, and selection source are surfaced.
Approval gates Risky tool or Code Mode actions require explicit operator approval.
Durable runs Long work survives waits, approvals, retries, and restart recovery paths.
Policy engine Tool access is evaluated through governed capability and risk boundaries.
Release lanes Visual, surface, auth, runtime, backup, API, memory, and docs lanes anchor claims.

Safe claims today

GoatCitadel supports governed local/cloud AI work, visible approvals, memory management, prompt quality checks, provider setup, integrations, desktop packaging, and repo-aware coding.

1.0 claims include Mission Control Next, Fastify gateway, shared contracts, durable mission-session Chat/Cowork/Code flow ownership, policy-governed tools, backup verify, visual regression coverage, API compatibility snapshots, and the extensions SDK boundary.

Not overclaimed

Some things are intentionally described as experimental or limited, especially hostile-code sandboxing and optional local inference.

Code Mode is governed trusted-code, not a hostile-code guarantee. NPU sidecar and mesh maturity are not readiness-bearing 1.0 signals. Remote MCP is constrained unless explicitly enabled.

Use Cases

Where GoatCitadel is useful

The strongest fit is someone who wants a serious AI workspace without handing over every decision to an opaque agent.

The strongest fit is a local-first operator workflow where model/provider choice, tool policy, artifacts, reproducibility, and human approvals matter.

Research

Turn a messy question into a structured answer

Use Chat for quick grounding, Cowork for deeper breakdowns, and Library for memory or knowledge sources.

Route from Chat into Cowork with preserved session context, attach knowledge, inspect trace, and export artifacts.

Build

Move from plan to code without losing proof

Open a Code thread, bind the repo, review diffs, run validation, and keep the user in control.

Use project binding, worktree state, Monaco panes, helper runs, patch export, and governed Code Mode metadata.

Operate

Keep runtime health and decisions visible

Ops shows activity, sessions, approvals, costs, runtime status, diagnostics, and backups.

Ops routes consume dashboard, health, realtime, costs, approvals, runtime lifecycle, durable, daemon, and diagnostic services.

Extend

Add skills, integrations, and add-ons carefully

New capabilities can be reviewed before they become something the AI can actually use.

The capability system separates inspectable proposals/candidates from callable activated capabilities, backed by lifecycle records and trust state.
